seo_title: Cost of Living in Sanya 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Sanya per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A tropical resort on Hainan Island: Russian citizens enjoy visa-free entry to Hainan for up to 30 days, a warm sea year-round and well-developed resort infrastructure. Downsides are the language barrier and China's internet restrictions.
pros: Visa-free entry to Hainan for up to 30 days
Tropics and a warm sea year-round
Clean air and good ecology on the island
A beach destination familiar to Russians
cons: China's internet restrictions (you need a VPN)
The winter high season drives prices up

faq.question: Do Russian citizens need a visa for Sanya?
faq.answer: No, Hainan Island offers visa-free entry for up to 30 days. For a longer stay you need a Chinese visa.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Sanya?
faq.answer: Moderately expensive in season, cheaper in summer. See the exact budget in the calculator above.

faq.question: What language is spoken in Sanya?
faq.answer: Chinese; there's little English, so a phone translator and the Russian-language signs in Dadonghai come in handy.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Sanya?
faq.answer: No. Almost all payments go through WeChat Pay and Alipay, and you'll also need yuan in cash.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Sanya?
faq.answer: Tropical: hot and humid, with swimming possible year-round; the peak season is winter.

faq.question: Do I need a VPN in Sanya?
faq.answer: Yes, many familiar sites and services are blocked in China — it's worth setting up a VPN in advance.

reviews.text: Sanya means a winter sea with no visa, clean and warm. The downsides are the language and payments only through Chinese apps, and you can't get anywhere without a VPN.
I wintered in Dadonghai: beaches, fruit, a Russian-speaking environment. It's a bit tricky without Chinese, and you have to work around the internet, but the sea is worth it.
